hook: The chemist who proved that germs cause disease, and made the first rabies vaccine.

pages.x: Louis Pasteur was born in 1822 in Dole, in eastern France, the son of a tanner, and grew up in Arbois. He was an ordinary student who loved drawing portraits of his family and friends.
At 25 he found that some crystals come in two mirror image forms, like a left and a right hand.
pages.fx: This founded a new branch of chemistry. It matters for medicines: a drug and its mirror twin can act on the body in very different ways.

pages.x: Asked why wine and beer went sour, he showed that fermentation and rotting are caused by living microbes. With flasks with long curved necks, he proved that microbes do not appear out of nothing.
pages.fx: His germ theory changed medicine: surgeons began to clean their hands and tools, and far fewer patients died.

pages.x: He found that heating wine to about 60 degrees for a short time kills the harmful microbes without spoiling the taste. The method was later used for milk.
pages.fx: Pasteurised milk has saved countless lives, and his name is printed on milk cartons around the world.

pages.x: Three of his five children died young, two of them of typhoid fever. The loss drove him to fight infectious disease. In 1868 a stroke paralysed his left side, but he kept working.

By accident, an old culture of chicken cholera, left out over the summer holidays, made chickens immune instead of sick. In 1881 he vaccinated sheep against anthrax in public: all the vaccinated sheep lived, the others died.
pages.fx: He had found how to make vaccines from weakened germs, a method used for many diseases ever since.

pages.x: In 1885 a mother brought him nine-year-old Joseph Meister, savaged by a mad dog. Rabies always killed. Pasteur, who was not even a doctor, risked his untested vaccine. The boy lived, and later became caretaker of the Pasteur Institute.
Gifts poured in from around the world to found the Pasteur Institute in Paris in 1888. Its scientists have since made many vaccines, and in 1983 discovered the virus that causes AIDS.
Pasteur proved that germs cause disease and spoil food. His work led to vaccines, pasteurisation and clean hospitals, saving millions of lives.
pts: Made the first vaccine against rabies
